newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian shares higher in brisk trade.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian shares higher in brisk trade.

text.p: Nigerian shares moved higher in brisk trade on Tuesday, dealers said.
The all share index closed at 6422.93 from 6422.79 on Monday.
Union Bank, one of the nation's big four, closed higher after favourable half-year results. The shares gained 32 kobo to close at 7.70 naira.
Guaranty Trust Bank remains the dearest stock in the sector at 12.75 naira after gaining 15 kobo. Investors see it as one of the most efficient banks in the country.
Oil marketing company shares continued to rise, as did food and cement sectors.
National Oil was up 40 kobo to 35.00 naira. Texaco rose 25 kobo to 25.00 naira, while Total ended 20 kobo higher at 45.30 naira.
West African Portland Cement finished 40 kobo higher at 31.20 naira.
Cadbury rose 20 kobo to 25.20 naira, Flour Mills of Nigeria rose the same amount to 10.20 naira.
Among conglomerates, PZ Industries rose 30 kobo to 36.00 naira, but CFAO and UAC finished lower with shares still looking for buyers.
CFAO dropped 10 kobo to 4.50 naira, while UAC lost five kobo to end at 11.25 naira.
Nigerian Breweries continued its slide, down 10 kobo to 12.80 naira.
Carnaud Metal Box was the sole faller in the troubled packaging sector, ending five kobo lower at 4.15 naira.
